title_en: Foshan Shunde Midea Washing Appliance Manufacturing Co., Ltd. v. Foshan Yunmi Electric Technology Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent
ruling_gist_en: In cases of disputes over patent infringement, where the alleged infringer presents evidence to prove that the accused infringing technical solution constitutes prior art, and thereby claims that its conduct does not constitute patent infringement, such defense constitutes a prior art defense. Given that prior art evidence predates the patent application date, in order to uphold the res judicata of effective judgments, regulate litigation order, avoid litigation ambush against the patentee and rendering the first and second instance proceedings moot, and to guide the parties to fully present their defenses and resolve disputes in the first and second instance proceedings, the prior art defense arguments and evidence raised by the alleged infringer for the first time during the retrial review procedure shall not be examined.

full_text_en:
Foshan Shunde Midea Washing Appliance Manufacturing Co., Ltd. v. Foshan Yunmi Electric Technology Co., Ltd., et al. — Dispute over Infringement of Utility Model Patent

【Ruling Summary】

In a patent infringement dispute, where the alleged infringer adduces evidence to prove that the alleged infringing technical solution falls within the prior art, and thereby claims that its conduct does not constitute patent infringement, such defense constitutes a prior art defense. Given that the prior art evidence all predates the patent application date, in order to maintain the res judicata effect of an effective judgment, standardize litigation order, avoid a surprise attack on the patentee and circumvent the first-instance and second-instance proceedings, and guide the parties to fully present their defenses and resolve disputes in the first-instance and second-instance proceedings, the prior art defense grounds and evidence raised by the alleged infringer for the first time during the retrial review procedure shall not be examined.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Shen No. 1

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance): Foshan Yunmi Electric Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: Unit 2, 1st Floor, Building 1, and 4th Floor, Building 7, No. 2 Xinxi Fourth Road North, Xiacun Village Committee, Lunjiao Subdistrict Office, Shunde District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Xiaoping, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Su Xiaonan, Attorney at Grandall Law Firm (Beijing).

Agent ad litem: Tang Yi, Attorney at Grandall Law Firm (Beijing).

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Foshan Shunde Midea Washing Appliance Manufacturing Co., Ltd. Domicile: Industrial Park, Beijiao Town, Shunde District, Foshan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Minfeng, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Wang Xiaofeng, Attorney at Zhejiang Zhiwuhe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Lijun, Attorney at Beijing Jincheng Tongda & Neal (Hangzhou) Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Shenzhen Kangzhi Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room B314, Huangjia Business Center, Baishilong Second District, Baishilong Community, Minzhi Subdistrict, Longhua District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Wan Zhihua, Executive Director.

Defendant at First Instance: Zhejiang Tmall Network Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 506, 5th Floor, Building 3, No. 969 Wenyi West Road, Wuchang Subdistrict, Yuhang District, Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Jiang Fan, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Li Yuan, Attorney at Beijing Jiarun Law Firm.

Regarding the dispute between the retrial applicant, Foshan Yunmi Electric Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yunmi Company), and the respondent, Foshan Shunde Midea Washing Appliance Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Midea Company), together with the defendants at first instance, Shenzhen Kangzhi Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kangzhi Company) and Zhejiang Tmall Network Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tmall Company), over infringement of a utility model patent, Yunmi Company, dissatisfied with the civil judgment rendered by the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province on March 20, 2019, in Case No. (2018) Zhe 01 Min Chu 1673, filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct the review, which has now been concluded.

Yunmi Company applied for retrial on the following grounds: 1. The basic facts found in the first-instance judgment lacked evidentiary support. Compared with the patented technical solution, the alleged infringing technical solution had several distinguishing features and did not fall within the scope of protection of claims 1-4 of the patent-in-suit, and therefore the relevant conduct did not constitute infringement. Specifically, the alleged infringing product did not include the technical features "a boss disposed opposite to the overlapping edge is formed on at least one of the outer door and the inner door" and "a boss is formed on the outer door around the mounting hole" as set forth in claim 1, nor did it include all the additional technical features of dependent claims 2-4; 2. New evidence in this case could overturn the first-instance judgment. After the conclusion of the original trial, Yunmi Company discovered a product at a user's home in Nanjing that had been publicly sold before the patent application date. This product could prove that the alleged infringing product adopted the prior art, and therefore Yunmi Company did not infringe, and the ruling of the first-instance judgment was erroneous. The above product was evidence discovered by Yunmi Company after the conclusion of the original trial due to objective reasons. Therefore, Yunmi Company requests the retrial court to examine the prior art defense raised based on this new evidence, in order to obtain a fair and just outcome. Requests: 1. To set aside the first-instance judgment; 2. To amend the judgment to find that Yunmi Company did not infringe Midea Company's patent rights, and to dismiss all of Midea Company's original claims; 3. To order Midea Company to bear the litigation costs of the original instance.

Midea Company submitted comments stating: 1. After the first-instance judgment was served, Yunmi Company did not appeal. After the first-instance judgment became effective, Yunmi Company directly applied for retrial. This conduct not only violates the basic civil trial principle of two-instance final adjudication in China, but also constitutes an abuse of litigation resources and violates the principle of good faith. The retrial request should not be supported; 2. The first-instance judgment correctly found that the technical solution of the alleged infringing product fell within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit; 3. The prior art defense raised by Yunmi Company is untenable. Request to dismiss Yunmi Company's retrial application.

This Court has ascertained the following facts upon review:

On April 21, 2015, Wuhu Midea Washing Appliance Manufacturing Co., Ltd. filed an application with the National Intellectual Property Administration for a utility model patent entitled "Door Assembly and Dishwasher Having Same" (i.e., the patent-in-suit). The patent was granted and announced on September 9, 2015, with patent number ZL201520245340.0, and the patentee was Wuhu Midea Washing Appliance Manufacturing Co., Ltd. On November 14, 2016, the patentee of the patent-in-suit was changed and registered to Midea Company. The patent-in-suit is currently valid. Some of the claims of the patent-in-suit are as follows:

1. A door assembly, characterized by comprising: an outer door, on which a mounting hole is formed; an inner door, arranged behind the outer door, an overlapping edge formed at a rim of the inner door, the overlapping edge abutting against the outer door, and a plurality of through holes arranged at intervals on the inner door; screws, a portion of each screw passing through the through hole in the inner door and extending into the mounting hole in the outer door to be threadedly connected with the outer door, the screws being multiple; wherein a boss disposed opposite to the overlapping edge is formed on at least one of the outer door and the inner door, and at least a portion of the overlapping edge and at least a portion of the boss are disposed on opposite sides of the screws.

2. The door assembly according to claim 1, characterized in that the boss is formed on the outer door, and the boss abuts against the inner door.

3. The door assembly according to claim 2, characterized in that a mounting portion extending toward an inner side of the outer door is formed on a side wall of the outer door, the mounting hole and the boss are formed on the mounting portion, the overlapping edge of the inner door abuts against the mounting portion, and the boss abuts against the inner door.

4. The door assembly according to claim 3, characterized in that the boss is formed on an inner edge of the mounting portion and adjacent to the mounting hole.

10. The door assembly according to claim 1, characterized in that the rim of the inner door is bent forward and inward to form the overlapping edge, and the through holes are disposed adjacent to the overlapping edge.

11. A dishwasher comprising the door assembly according to any one of claims 1-10.

Yunmi Company acknowledged that the physical dishwasher product alleged to be infringing, obtained by Midea Company through notarized purchase, was manufactured and sold by Yunmi Company. Midea Company specified that it asserted rights based on claims 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, and 11 of the patent-in-suit, and for claim 11, it relies on claims 1-4 and 10. Midea Company claimed that the alleged infringing technical solution was identical to the technical solution described in the above claims. Yunmi Company and Tmall Company both disputed the technical features related to the boss asserted by Midea Company, contending that the technical features of the alleged infringing product were different from those of the patent-in-suit. Yunmi Company argued that its alleged infringing product did not have the boss of Midea Company's patent-in-suit, did not recognize the positional relationship of the opposite sides, and did not accept the technical feature that the boss and the overlapping edge were located on both sides of the screw. Yunmi Company did not raise a prior art defense in the original proceedings.

The first-instance court found that the technical features of the alleged infringing product, the dishwasher, were identical to those of claims 1-4, 10, and 11 (referring to claims 1-4, 10) of the patent-in-suit, and thus fell within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit, constituting infringement. Yunmi Company, without the permission of the patentee, offered for sale, sold, and manufactured the alleged infringing product for the purpose of production and operation; Kangzhi Company, without the permission of the patentee, offered for sale and sold the alleged infringing product; both parties infringed Midea Company's patent-in-suit. Midea Company's claim for an injunction, destruction of infringing products, damages, and reasonable expenses incurred to stop the infringement against Yunmi Company and Kangzhi Company was in accordance with the law and was supported within a reasonable scope. Since Midea Company did not submit evidence proving that Tmall Company had a joint infringement intent with Yunmi Company and Kangzhi Company, Midea Company's claim that Tmall Company also constituted infringement was untenable. Midea Company failed to effectively prove its losses and the infringer's profits, and Yunmi Company and Kangzhi Company also failed to provide effective evidence of their profits from the infringement. Midea Company's request for statutory damages was in accordance with the law. With respect to reasonable expenses, considering the specific circumstances of the case, the work performed by the attorneys in this case, and the relevant evidence such as notarized documents and physical evidence submitted at the time of filing the lawsuit, attorney fees, notarization fees, and other reasonable expenses were partially supported within a reasonable range.

In summary, the first-instance judgment ordered: 1. Yunmi Company to immediately cease the acts of manufacturing, selling, and offering for sale the alleged infringing products that fell within the scope of protection of Midea Company's patent-in-suit, and to destroy the infringing products; 2. Kangzhi Company to immediately cease the acts of selling and offering for sale the alleged infringing products that fell within the scope of protection of Midea Company's patent-in-suit, and to destroy the infringing products; 3. Yunmi Company to pay Midea Company economic losses and reasonable expenses incurred to stop the infringement, totaling RMB 500,000; Kangzhi Company to pay Midea Company economic losses and reasonable expenses incurred to stop the infringement, totaling RMB 20,000; 4. To dismiss Midea Company's other claims.

After the first-instance judgment was rendered, none of the parties appealed. The first-instance judgment became effective after the appeal period expired.

Upon review, this Court finds that the issues in this case are: (1) Whether the alleged infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. (2) Whether the prior art defense grounds and evidence raised by Yunmi Company for the first time in the retrial procedure, which were not raised in the original proceedings, should be accepted and examined.

(1) Whether the alleged infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit.

Article 59, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) provides that the scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of its claims. The description and drawings may be used to interpret the content of the claims. Therefore, to determine whether the alleged infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit, a comparison must be made between the technical solution described in the claims asserted by the patentee and the alleged infringing technical solution, i.e., comparing the technical features possessed by the alleged infringing technical solution with the technical features of the patent described in the claims. If the alleged infringing technical solution completely covers all the technical features of the patent claims, then the alleged infringing product falls within the scope of patent protection, which includes the scope determined by features identical or equivalent to the patent technical features. With respect to the differences raised by Yunmi Company and Tmall Company, this Court finds upon review that the alleged infringing technical solution comprises an outer door, a mounting hole, an inner door, an overlapping edge, through holes, screws, a boss disposed opposite to the overlapping edge formed on at least one of the outer door and the inner door, and a boss formed on the outer door around the mounting hole. Therefore, the alleged infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of claims 1-4 of the patent-in-suit. At the same time, the rim of the inner door of the alleged infringing product is bent forward and inward to form the overlapping edge, and the through holes are disposed adjacent to the overlapping edge. The alleged infringing technical solution also falls within the scope of protection of claim 10 and claim 11 of the patent-in-suit. In conclusion, the technical solution of the alleged infringing dishwasher product is identical to the technical features of claims 1-4, 10, and 11 of the patent-in-suit, and has already fallen within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. The first-instance judgment correctly ordered Yunmi Company to bear civil liability to cease the infringement. Although it was improper not to distinguish between damages and reasonable expenses, this does not affect the outcome of this case.

(2) Whether the prior art defense grounds and evidence raised by Yunmi Company for the first time in the retrial procedure, which were not raised in the original proceedings, should be accepted and examined.

Article 62 of the Patent Law provides that in a patent infringement dispute, if the alleged infringer has evidence to prove that the technology or design it implements belongs to the prior art or prior design, it does not constitute patent infringement. According to the above provision, in a patent infringement dispute, where the alleged infringer adduces evidence to prove that the alleged infringing technical solution is prior art, and thereby claims that its conduct does not constitute patent infringement, such defense constitutes a prior art defense.

In this case, Yunmi Company filed an application for retrial with this Court on the ground that it discovered new evidence after the first-instance judgment became effective. Applying for retrial refers to a procedural act where a party, believing that a civil judgment, ruling, or mediation statement that has already taken legal effect rendered by a people's court is indeed erroneous, requests the initiation of retrial proceedings to set aside or modify the effective judgment. The legislative purpose of retrial proceedings is to balance the protection of the parties' right to apply for retrial with the maintenance of the res judicata effect and stability of effective judgments, thereby upholding judicial justice. Since the initiation of retrial proceedings directly affects the validity of effective judgments, in order to maintain the stability of the legal order established by effective judgments, the grounds for retrial should be limited to matters such as significant defects in the litigation evidence of the original judgment or serious deficiencies in the litigation procedure that hinder the parties' fundamental litigation rights. According to Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), a people's court shall conduct a retrial if there is new evidence sufficient to overturn the original judgment or ruling. Article 10 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Trial Supervision Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China further defines new evidence for retrial, including "evidence that objectively existed before the conclusion of the original trial but was discovered after the conclusion of the original trial."

This Court holds that submitting new evidence in a retrial application without having raised a prior art defense in the original proceedings should not fall under the above circumstances. The reasons are as follows:

First, with respect to the exercise of adjudicative power, whether to ensure the stability of court judgments or to prevent abuse of procedural rights, courts should confer substantive effect on judgments formed through proper trial procedures. That is, once a judgment has taken effect, it should have res judicata effect, making the litigation reach a final conclusion, ensuring its stability, and not allowing it to be easily overturned. Conversely, easily reopening proceedings for an already effective case would not only make it difficult to have a truly final judgment but would also seriously damage judicial authority. The prior art evidence submitted by Yunmi Company to this Court at the time of applying for retrial all predates the patent application date and could have been obtained during the original trial. In form, Yunmi Company's application for retrial is based on new evidence, but in substance, it amounts to raising a new defense ground. If the retrial application procedure were to accept the prior art defense and new evidence raised for the first time by the alleged infringer, it would undermine the res judicata effect of the effective judgment. The prior art defense is a unique defense right in patent infringement civil disputes and is a defense right enjoyed by the alleged infringer under the law. Since the prior art defense is clearly provided for in the Patent Law, the alleged infringer should raise it in the first-instance or second-instance proceedings in accordance with the law. However, if the alleged infringer fails to exercise its defense right in the first-instance or second-instance proceedings and raises it only in the retrial application procedure, this not only violates the principle of procedural fairness but also damages the res judicata effect of the effective judgment, contradicting the legislative purpose of retrial proceedings to balance the protection of the parties' right to apply for retrial and the maintenance of the res judicata effect and stability of effective judgments.

Second, as a special remedy beyond the two-instance final adjudication procedure, the retrial application procedure has its unique litigation value. If, after the normal civil litigation procedure has concluded, effective judgments easily enter retrial proceedings, their validity would remain in a state of flux for a long time, and the rights and obligations of the parties would remain unstable, making it difficult to achieve stability in social and economic order. Patent rights, as important property rights, play a very significant role in current economic life. In different technical fields such as information and communications, biomedicine, electrical equipment, and computer software, many key patented technologies directly affect the lifeblood of industries and technological development. In the process of industry competition and enterprise development, a patentee obtaining a favorable effective judgment through patent infringement litigation can not only effectively curb infringement and obtain high license fees and damages to compensate for research and development costs and provide financial support for subsequent research, but also gain and maintain a long-term competitive advantage. On the other hand, the public, through effective judgments, can determine the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit, thereby safely engaging in market activities such as manufacturing and selling while avoiding the patented technical solution, and can continue innovative research and development on the basis of the patented technical solution. Therefore, whether for the patentee, its competitors, or the public, the stability of the state of patent infringement disputes is of great significance. Patent infringement litigation procedures often take a long time. When a people's court makes a civil judgment confirming the legal relationship in dispute, the patentee and its competitors and other industry practitioners who rely on that judgment will quickly stabilize and arrange their production and business activities in accordance with the rights and obligations and relevant legal facts determined by that judgment. If the retrial review procedure were to be entered based on existing prior art evidence that was already available, it would destabilize the already time-consuming and stable economic order again, which is detrimental to the normal conduct of production and business activities.

Third, considering the value of the two-instance final adjudication system, ordinary civil litigation in China adopts a two-instance final adjudication system. A party who believes that a judgment or ruling that has become final is indeed erroneous may only apply for retrial in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, but the execution of the judgment or ruling shall not be suspended. The two-instance final adjudication system is conducive for higher-level people's courts to supervise the trial work of lower-level people's courts, promptly correct erroneous judgments, and protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties. It also facilitates the parties' participation in litigation, allows them to fully exercise their defense rights, quickly resolves disputes, and provides timely judicial remedies for the parties' damaged rights and interests, preventing the case from becoming a burden due to prolonged delay. If the retrial application procedure were to examine the prior art defense grounds and evidence that the alleged infringer did not raise in the first-instance and second-instance proceedings, it would inevitably have a significant impact on the first-instance and second-instance procedures, effectively circumventing those procedures and undermining the value of the two-instance final adjudication litigation system.

Fourth, from the perspective of equality of the parties in civil proceedings, allowing the review of a prior art defense and its evidence raised for the first time at the retrial stage would violate the principle of equality in litigation. Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law requires that a plaintiff's complaint must include specific claims, facts, and reasons. Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases provides that the patentee shall finalize its patent claims before the conclusion of the court debate at the first instance. According to the Civil Procedure Law and the above judicial interpretation, the subject matter of the action between the plaintiff and the defendant in a patent infringement lawsuit shall be determined at the first instance to ensure the balance of litigation between the parties and enhance the parties' expectations of the litigation outcome, thereby safeguarding procedural justice. Permitting the alleged infringer to raise a prior art defense and its evidence at the retrial review stage that were not asserted in the first or second instance proceedings would result in a litigation ambush against the patentee and seriously undermine the requirements of procedural justice.

In summary, the retrial ground based on the prior art defense raised by Yunmi Company should not be accepted. Since none of Yunmi Company's retrial grounds can be sustained, this court does not support its retrial request.

Pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Paragraph 2 of Article 395 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court rules as follows:

The retrial application of Foshan Yunmi Electric Technology Co., Ltd. is rejected.

Judge: She Chaoyang
